title: The Gunshot at the Sunflower Estate
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention, matching the old wiki-derived case file's choice to drop Kogoro even though he is briefly named a 'suspect' by the local police in the source dialogue. The old case file's culprit (Amamori/s2) is confirmed correct against the full transcript -- no discrepancy with label.murderer_id. What the old file missed: (1) the theft of the rifle from the victim himself a week prior, (2) that the pine-tree rifle rig was physically placed there *before* the evening rain (6:00-6:30 PM) while Amamori's 7:25 PM 'coal run' only involved a ~1-minute action at the building's base (hooking the pre-laid wire onto an oiled decorative ledge with an extendable newspaper-and-tape pole) -- the mud-on-dry-wire contradiction is the actual key clue, reduced in the old file to a vague 'mechanical delay' fact; (3) Amamori's fabricated 3-month stalker-photo campaign against the victim, invented to misdirect the investigation toward an outside intruder; (4) the backstory motive itself -- Amamori, not Kanazawa, designed the Shanghai Museum of Modern Art submission that won Kanazawa an international prize, and Kanazawa threatened Amamori into silence over it. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The fishing wire and trigger were caked in mud when found, but the pine-tree area saw heavy rain from roughly 6:00-6:30 PM that should have washed any mud away if the mechanism had been set up and pulled around the same time as the shot (7:35 PM). This timing contradiction proves the rifle/wire rig was placed at the tree before the rain (i.e., before the guests even arrived) and was fired later by a slow, remote, oil-assisted delay mechanism -- not by an outside intruder physically present at the tree during the shooting window.

edges.motive_type: professional (Kanazawa publicly took credit for Amamori's prize-winning Shanghai Museum of Modern Art design and threatened him into silence)

edges.detail: After Amamori objected to Kanazawa taking public credit for his design, Kanazawa warned him that his position at the firm depended on staying quiet.
Begins mailing himself-authored 'stalker' photographs to Kanazawa weekly, three months before the murder.
Steals the rifle from Kanazawa's own collection approximately one week before the murder; Kanazawa reports it stolen.
Ties the stolen rifle and trigger to the fishing wire and plants it at the pine tree before the evening rain begins, hours before the party.
Hayashida leaves the party ~7:20 PM to fetch beer, gone about 5 minutes.

Leaves the party ~7:25 PM under the pretext of fetching coal; in under a minute, hooks the pre-laid fishing wire onto the oiled second-floor decoration using the newspaper-sheet pole, arming the delayed-pull mechanism, then returns to the party.
Uses the same newspaper-and-tape pole as his cover story's coal-carrying stick.
Kanazawa goes up alone to the second-floor library at 7:29 PM to watch his usual live Chinese-lesson broadcast.
Mitsuko leaves the party for the bathroom at 7:30 PM, returns about 5 minutes later.

edges.method: delayed, remotely-triggered rifle shot: a weighted fishing line hooked to an oiled decorative ledge slid down over roughly 10 minutes before finally pulling the trigger of a rifle tied at the base of a pine tree 10 meters from the building

edges.detail: Body discovered ~7:39-7:40 PM after the door, locked from the inside, is broken down with an axe.
Leads the on-site investigation with the Shizuoka Prefectural Police after the body is found.
